notes: Matched 113 of 158 (A) and 121 (B) units by overlapping or adjacent anchors; every one-coder unit (45 A, 8 B) was checked against the saved text and kept, none dropped. Main disagreements: (1) unit_stance (agreement 0.84), mostly whether a condition on permitted use is permit vs encourage/neutral and restrict vs prohibit for data-input bans; resolved by taking the position the single rule takes on AI use. (2) policy_type (0.88): P09 vs P66 for explaining rules, P56 vs P61 vs P77 for scope and framework statements, P12 vs P13, P02 vs P15, and three cases where neither coder's type fit (permission gate before graded use, dispute route, self-reflection question), recoded UNCOVERED with both coders' notes kept. (3) actor (0.89): who a guide to instructors binds, resolved by who the sentence applies to. (4) Granularity: coder A split lists (approved tools, high-risk examples) into one unit each and coder B often merged adjacent sentences into long normalized policies; kept separate units and set policy to null when the anchor states the rule. Stance agreed for all 4 documents (delegates). Extra field agree_unit_stance added.
